On Wed, Jul 14, 2029 at 08:20 AM Hannah Schmitt wrote:
> Mike — thanks for the heads up and the log. I’m escalating to SRE and Eng now.

Quick diagnostics from our side (short summary):
- Telemetry: A 3x increase in prefix token fanout and sustained KV cache churn starting 07:48 PDT.
- Error pattern: majority 502/503 tied to backend model-worker "enqueue_backpressure" and repeated KV cache evictions.
- Capacity: reserved GPU pool still shows allocated instances, but GPU util is at ~95% and CPU-bound scheduler queues show growing backlog for short-lived requests.
- Hypothesis: sudden token-level surge causing inefficient batching + KV cache thrash -> runtime falling back to slower execution path, which in turn fills per-instance request queues and triggers 5xx as requests time out.

Immediate mitigations I recommend:
1) Temporary safety: drop the per-tenant max_concurrent_requests to 60% and enforce aggressive short timeouts to shed tail load.
2) Enable burst authorization to spin up warm dedicated nodes (if allowed by contract) for next 30–90 minutes while we investigate root cause.
3) Pin model variant to the previous kernel/quantization profile if a rollout occurred in the last 36 hours (we’re checking deploy history now).

I’m attaching a quick QPS chart we pulled from internal dashboards (qps_kpi_chart.png). Marcus, can you start the bridge and capture heap/KV-hit ratios? Naomi, please prepare an impact calc for potential credits.

-Karthik
Lead Inference Engineer

Date: 2029-07-14T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: containment and next steps (VelociPay)

Mike — quick summary from today’s incident (timeline / what we did / next steps):

What happened:
- Starting ~07:48 PDT we observed a token-level surge that caused excessive KV cache evictions and inefficient batching in the Dedicated pool serving VelociPay. That led to request queueing and an elevated 502/503 rate for roughly 90 minutes.

Immediate containment completed by 10:20 PDT:
- Short-term request-shedding (reduced concurrent requests) applied at 08:40 PDT.
- Emergency burst authorization executed at 08:50 PDT (+2 warm nodes) which reduced per-instance queueing.
- No deploy rollbacks were required; we pinned the model variant while diagnostics continued.

Customer impact and remediation:
- Impact window: 07:48–10:20 PDT (approx 2h32m, with highest error-rate in first 90 min).
- Attachments: opstrace_log_excerpt.txt and qps_kpi_chart.png (diagnostic artifacts).
- We are preparing a full RCA; preliminary root cause points to transient token-surge-driven KV cache thrash compounded by aggressive batching heuristics.

Compensation and next steps:
- Naomi will send a proposed credit amount based on observed token loss and SLA terms by EOD.
- Engineering will deliver a targeted mitigation (KV cache tuning + revised batching thresholds) in a canary next week; we’ll share the rollout plan and invite a VelociPay test window.
- We will schedule a follow-up stakeholder call with VelociPay leadership and our CTO if you’d like (proposed: tomorrow 10:00 PDT).

Links: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-20290714-0143 (live notes), https://drive.redwood.com/velocipay/diagnostics-qps.png

Apologies for the disruption — we take this seriously. I’ll keep you posted with the RCA draft.

—Hannah
Sr. AM, Redwood Inference
